newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE to crack down on ships busting Iraq sanctions.
newsitem.headline: UAE to crack down on ships busting Iraq sanctions.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates vowed on Wednesday to crack down on an increasing number of UAE-flagged vessels trying to bust U.N. sanctions imposed on Iraq, the official news agency WAM said.

The decision was taken during a meeting of several cabinet ministers to tackle what the agency termed "an increasing number of violations regarding sanctions imposed on Iraq by ships carrying the UAE flag".
An official spokesman later told WAM the gathering decided to "take necessary and appropriate measures regarding this issue in line with relevant U.N. resolutions".
He gave no further details. Officials and U.S. Navy inspectors were not immediately available for comment.

The U.S. Navy is part of a multinational force which checks shipping in the Gulf to enforce the U.N. trade embargo imposed on Iraq after its 1990 invasion of Kuwait. It occasionally intercepts ships carrying banned goods to and from Iraq.
It said in January it intercepted a UAE-flagged cargo ship carrying computers, vehicle parts and tyres in violation of U.N. sanctions.
